subject: Urgent: NimbusPay p95 latency breach after model7delta deploy - mitigation plan
messages:
From: Alice Moreno <alice@nimbuspay.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95 spike after model7delta deploy - looking for immediate mitigation

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing a sharp p95 latency increase around 08:30 PT after you rolled model7delta for our traffic. The symptom is requests timing out at the application layer (~10s) which is breaking our checkout flows. Our engineering team traced some of the traces to long KV cache misses and higher token decode time. This is now impacting ~6% of sessions and increasing conversion drop.

Can Redwood activate an immediate fallback or split traffic back to the previous variant while we investigate? We need either a quick mitigation or an agreed SL carveout window. We have a contract clause for emergency rollbacks but want to avoid churn if there is a config fix.

Attachments: nimbuspay-slo-report.pdf (SLO screenshots), latency_trace_20280720.json (sample traces)

Thanks,
Alice
Head of Platform
NimbusPay

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Alice Moreno <alice@nimbuspay.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike after model7delta deploy - looking for immediate mitigation

Alice — thanks for the quick heads up and for the attachments. I’m escalating now to SRE and Product.

Immediate plan (short):
- I’ll open a mitigation playbook and request an automated traffic split to previous variant (model7gamma) for 100% of checkout traffic for NimbusPay if the SRE team cannot validate a quick fix within 30 minutes.
- Ben, can you validate capacity/burst on their Dedicated pool and whether we can route to a cold-warm pool to absorb the spike?
- Karthik, please advise on policy for an emergency rollback vs a soft traffic diversion (customer preference is to avoid full rollback if we can preserve session continuity).

We’ll keep you updated every 15 minutes.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike after model7delta deploy - looking for immediate mitigation

Vanessa / team — quick technical readout from SRE: traces show two correlated signals after model7delta activation for this tenant:
1) Increased KV cache churn for long sessions (cache hit rate dropped ~18%).
2) Higher per-token decode time on A100 nodes for sequences > 512.

Mitigation options we can enact immediately:
- Option A (fast): Traffic diversion — split 80/20 back to model7gamma for 30m and evaluate p95. This preserves sessions for 80% and reduces user impact quickly.
- Option B (aggressive): Full traffic reroute to model7gamma (effectively a soft rollback) — lowest risk to SLA but will change prediction surface for a subset of recent features. Requires a notice to the customer for any data-drift sensitive integrations.
- Option C: Autoscale Dedicated pool + force-hot cache priming (30m window) — buys time but costs will spike; uncertain hit on p95 during scale.

My recommendation: Option A now, with 30-minute telemetry window; if p95 does not return within that window, escalate to Option B. I’ll stand by to flip the traffic rule if you authorize.

Attachments: fallback-runbook-v2.md

Ben Carter
Lead Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike after model7delta deploy - looking for immediate mitigation

Agree with Ben. A phased diversion is lower risk operationally. A couple notes on governance: we have an internal gate that requires sales lead + product approval for full rollbacks that affect model selection on customer traffic. Given the impact and the contract clause, I approve the phased diversion now. If the phased diversion fails after 30 minutes, we will need a formal rollback authorization which I will sign off on (I’ll ping GL if needed).

Please record the decision in HubSpot (deal D-98721) and tag this as an "emergency mitigation". Ben — please track cost delta if you enable autoscale.

Karthik
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Alice Moreno <alice@nimbuspay.com>, Jack Liu <jack@payments-ops.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Jul 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike after model7delta deploy - mitigation plan enacted

Alice / Jack — summary of actions and next steps: 
- At 15:10 PT on Jul 20 we activated Option A: phased traffic diversion (80% -> model7gamma, 20% stayed on model7delta) for checkout traffic scoped to NimbusPay.
- Observed p95 fall from 1.2s to 320ms within 12 mins for diverted traffic; overall incident impact reduced to <0.5% sessions.
- We kept monitoring for 2 hours. No telemetry indicated regressions on model7gamma. After assessing risk, product approved a controlled soft rollback to route 100% of checkout traffic to model7gamma at 17:40 PT. That soft rollback is still in effect.
- We did not need to autoscale Dedicated pool. Cost delta was negligible.

Next steps:
1) Redwood SRE will run a deeper perf profile of model7delta (kernel-level traces, KV cache policy) and share findings by Tue 24 Jul 18:00 PT.
2) Product will create a postmortem and a list of mitigations before re-promoting model7delta.
3) We’ll schedule a sync with NimbusPay on Wed 25 Jul 09:00 PT to review root cause and remediation timeline.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/98721; Runbook: https://redwood-internal.internal/runbooks/fallback-v2

Attachments: fallback-runbook-v2.md

Thanks for the patience — we’ll follow up with the postmortem ASAP.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
